A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DeepRAG and provide readable methods, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The retained and relocated material can be matched reliably, with no essential reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on five QA datasets, retrieval-efficiency measurements, knowledge-boundary analyses, and training ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and adds MuSiQue evaluations, a 32B model evaluation, runtime measurements, and reinforcement-learning results.

M1.justification: The original binary-tree synthesis, imitation learning, and chain-of-calibration pipeline remains. Section 5.3 and Appendix C.5 add an alternative Stage II using GRPO initialized from DeepRAG-Imi, with a reward incorporating correctness, formatting, and retrieval cost. This substantially extends the training procedure; the original loss equations are retained in Appendix B.

E1.justification: v2 adds MuSiQue as an out-of-distribution multi-hop QA benchmark while retaining the original five datasets and the HotpotQA/2WikiMultihopQA training coverage. This extends evaluation within the existing open-domain QA scope.

E2.justification: Search-o1 changes from a related-work citation in v1 to an evaluated comparator in v2 Table 1, implemented using DeepSeek-R1 distillation models. Existing comparators remain, including QwQ-32B-preview and gpt-4o-turbo, whose comparison moves to Appendix C.3.

E3.justification: v2 adds Qwen-2.5-32B evaluations, a GRPO training experiment, and per-query runtime measurement. Section 4.3 also revises the reported CAG retrieval setting: v1 describes Wikipedia generally, whereas v2 specifies dataset-provided up-to-date passages for CAG. This is a reported protocol revision; unchanged CAG scores do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an RL training-dynamics analysis of F1 versus retrieval frequency in Figure 3 and runtime profiling within the efficiency analysis. Existing inference-strategy, decomposition, calibration, and case-study analyses remain. However, v1 Tables 7–8's separate HotpotQA/2Wiki ablation breakdowns disappear; aggregate ablation comparisons remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run evaluation counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. v2's eight rollouts per prompt describe GRPO training, not repeated evaluations or uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Table 1 adds substantial MuSiQue, Search-o1, and 32B results; Llama DeepRAG obtains 22.50 EM and 30.40 F1 on MuSiQue. All 230 original five-dataset EM/F1 entries remain unchanged. The Llama average changes from 47.67 to 44.13 because coverage expands to six datasets. v2 also adds runtime values, including 0.50 seconds per WebQuestions item for DeepRAG, and RL learning curves, while removing individual-dataset ablation entries.

T1.justification: Appendix C.5 introduces a formal RL reward: incorrect answers receive 0 or 0.1 depending on format, and correct answers receive 1 minus 0.1 times the retrieval count capped at five. The original MDP formulation and training losses are otherwise retained, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The central claims about adaptive retrieval, query decomposition, and knowledge-boundary calibration remain. The abstract changes the claimed accuracy improvement from 21.99% to 26.4%, and the conclusion adopts 26.4%; however, v2's introduction still states 21.99%, leaving the revised headline claim inconsistent.

C2.justification: v2 adds specific limitations concerning exact-match-based data construction and absent knowledge-graph/tool integration. It interprets the new RL curves as evidence that the reward encourages accurate, economical retrieval. The explanation for CoT-Retrieve's CAG advantage shifts from simple one-hop questions to the need to retrieve frequently for time-sensitive questions.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents Qwen-2.5-72B generating decomposition queries and retrieved answers, with the target model generating parametric answers. It adds DeepRAG and RL code links, eight-H20 timing hardware, and GRPO settings of batch size 32 and eight rollouts per prompt. These substantially improve implementation disclosure; the PDFs do not establish that the synthesis teacher itself changed between versions.

R1.justification: Related work adds a contrast with RL retrieval methods, including Search-R1, R1-Searcher, and SmartRAG, emphasizing their treatment of retrieval efficiency. Additional reasoning, GRPO, and benchmark references support the extensions, while Bian et al. is removed. The existing adaptive-retrieval, reasoning, and knowledge-boundary positioning largely remains.

P1.justification: v2 extensively rewrites the introduction and method exposition, corrects the title's 'Retrieval' to 'Retrieve,' and reorganizes the analysis. Training objectives, strong-model comparisons, detailed ablation discussion, and the case study move into restructured appendices. New RL and limitations sections further change the narrative organization.

P2.justification: Table 1 gains MuSiQue columns and a 32B model block, while the main efficiency table gains timing and focuses on WebQuestions; the original full table moves to the appendix. v2 adds an RL plot, splits the original two-panel ablation figure into separate figures, relocates several tables and the case-study figure, and removes the detailed per-dataset ablation tables.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens assessment of efficiency and generalization through measured runtime, MuSiQue and 32B evaluations, and clearer disclosure of the synthesis teacher. Implementation information and explicit limitations improve transparency. These benefits are tempered by lost per-dataset ablation detail and inconsistent 26.4% versus 21.99% headline claims. With the original benchmark scores unchanged, the evidence supports a limited overall quality improvement.
